sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Co-immunoprecipitation pull-down assay: tagged CRB1 was expressed and successfully pulled down interaction partners, demonstrating protein expression and preserved protein-protein interaction capability. Surface localization and primary biological function (cell polarity) were NOT MEASURED.
sites.rationale: L1 reports N-terminal FLAG and HA tags on full-length CRB1 expressed in HEK293T cells. CRB1 topology places the N-terminus extracellularly (residues 26-1347) and the C-terminus intracellularly (residues 1369-1406), so the N-terminal tag is the sole extracellular terminus available. The signal peptide spans residues 1-25 (last residue S at position 25), so the tag must be inserted after residue 25 to avoid being cleaved with the signal peptide; the mature N-terminus begins at F26. Python-verified: seq[25]='S', seq[26]='F', and the insert site is 1322 residues from the TM boundary (well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint). Full-length CRB1 with N-terminal FLAG and HA tags expressed in HEK293T cells; used for co-immunoprecipitation pull-down assays. CRB1 has a single extracellular N-terminus (residues 26-1347) and an intracellular C-terminus (residues 1369-1406), so the N-terminal tag lands on the extracellular face after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 25.

sources.claim: To generate N-terminal (CRB1) and C-terminal (CRB2, CRB3, and GFP) FLAG- and HA-tagged constructs, cDNA was amplified by PCR using primers carrying attb1 and attb2 recombination site overhangs.

literature_notes: The ledger contains one line (L1) for CRB1, reporting N-terminal FLAG and HA tags on full-length CRB1 in HEK293T cells for co-IP. No residue number is named, but CRB1 has exactly one extracellular terminus (N-terminal, residues 26-1347), making the position topology-derived at insert_after_residue=25 (after signal peptide cleavage). The C-terminal tags mentioned in the same paper are applied to CRB2, CRB3, and GFP — not CRB1 — consistent with CRB1's C-terminus being intracellular (residues 1369-1406), recorded in other_positions. No internal loop insertions are supported by the ledger. Validation is detected_only because the paper reports co-IP pull-down (protein-protein interaction preserved) but does not explicitly measure surface localization or CRB1's primary biological function (cell polarity/retinal lamination).

literature_other_positions.note: CRB1 C-terminus (residue 1406, topology 1369-1406 intracellular) is not a surface site; the same paper applies C-terminal tags to CRB2, CRB3, and GFP but explicitly uses N-terminal tags for CRB1, consistent with the intracellular location of CRB1's C-terminus.
